recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to light gray #F0F0F0. Use one sans-serif font family throughout; all body text black #000000.
2. Place a text box top-center with the title 'Recall' in large bold red #D00000 (largest text on the slide).
3. Place a yellow circle (exact shade unspecified; use #FFD700) in the top-right corner containing the number '11' in black.
4. Upper-left: draw a gray #E0E0E0 rectangle with a red #D00000 underline along its bottom edge. Inside, line 1: 'Correctly Classified (as Positive)'; line 2: 'Total objects that should be retrieved (Actually Positive)'.
5. Directly below the gray strip: draw a cream #F5F5DC rectangle. Line 1: 'Meaning' in bold red #D00000. Line 2: 'Does the classifier miss any of Positive Objects ?' in black, with the word 'miss' in red italic and the word 'Positive' underlined in blue #0000FF.
6. Below the meaning box on the left: draw a white #FFFFFF rectangle with a red #D00000 border containing 'Recall =' followed by a stacked fraction: numerator 'TP', horizontal fraction bar, denominator 'TP + FN', all in black.
7. Immediately to the right of the formula box (center of slide): draw a light-blue #E3F2FD rectangle with line 1 'Recall = 28/(28+2)' and line 2 '=93.3%' in black.
8. Below the formula box: draw a beige #F5E6D3 speech bubble with a pointer pointing left, containing 'Positive Classified as +ive' in black.
9. Next to it: draw a second beige #F5E6D3 speech bubble with a pointer pointing right, containing 'Positive Classified as -ive' in black.
10. Directly below the two speech bubbles: add one line of red #D00000 italic text: 'All Positive Samples in the Dataset'.
11. Bottom-left: draw a rectangle filled #E3F2FD with a blue #0000FF border containing two black sentences: 'Higher Recall means I HIGHLY trust you if you said I picked ALL Positive Objects.' and 'It Does NOT mean All you said Positive are Actually Positive'. Bold the words 'HIGHLY' and 'NOT'.
12. Top-right (below the slide-number circle): build confusion matrix table 1: header row 'Predicted as' spanning two columns 'P' and 'N'; a left row-header column labeled 'Actual' with rows 'P' and 'N'; the 2x2 grid cells read TP (top-left, green #00AA00 fill), FN (top-right, red #FF0000 fill), FP (bottom-left, red #FF0000 fill), TN (bottom-right, green #00AA00 fill); black cell text on white #FFFFFF table base.
13. Directly below table 1: build confusion matrix table 2 with the identical header structure ('Predicted as', columns 'P'/'N', row header 'Actual', rows 'P'/'N'). Row P: cell under column P shows '28' inside a purple #800080 circle; cell under column N shows '2' inside a red #FF0000 circle. Row N: cells '30' and '40' with green #00AA00 fill (source states green fill for both; see validation note).
14. Bottom-right, left tree, labeled 'Positive' in red #D00000: draw root circle '30' filled red #D00000 with a small line-drawing airplane icon directly above it; draw left child circle '28' filled red #D00000 with label 'TP' and right child circle '2' filled green #00AA00 with label 'FN'; connect root to both children with straight black lines.
15. Bottom-right, right tree, labeled 'Negative' in green #00AA00: draw root circle '70' filled green #00AA00 with a small line-drawing airplane icon directly above it; draw left child circle '40' filled green #00AA00 with label 'TN' and right child circle '30' filled red #D00000 with label 'FP'; connect root to both children with straight black lines.
